title: Use an explicit named-session lifecycle for managed jobs
summary: For multi-stage managed work, use a stable session name and an explicit lifecycle: allocate -> verify session -> stage secrets/inputs -> install -> execute -> collect outputs -> stop. Current upstream operator guidance recommends always naming sessions because autogenerated or ambiguous sessions make later commands unsafe. One-shot colab run is useful for simple ephemeral scripts, but explicit sessions are easier to evidence and recover when a job has separate install, upload, execution and download stages.
evidence_note: Current google-colab-cli upstream operator documentation: colab new -s <name>, colab exec -s <name> -f <script>, colab stop -s <name>. Live Gemma jobs used stable names such as gemma-oorexx-recovery and gemma-oorexx-regrade and cleaned them on every failure.
invariants: Managed automation uses a deterministic session name rather than relying on the only-active-session shortcut.
Stop is idempotent cleanup, not a success-only action.
Do not interpret keep-alive as durability; the VM remains ephemeral.
